claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation. Let me ask you about the child or children you're inquiring about.

**What is the age of the child/children you're claiming for?** 

Please tell me:
1. How many children do you have that you want to claim for?
2. What are their ages?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation. The key age categories are:
- **Under 16** - generally qualify automatically
- **16 to 19** - may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over** - generally don't qualify

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old. That means he falls into the 16-19 age category, so I need to check some additional eligibility requirements.

Let me get the details for the next step:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, for Alex who is 17, I need to know about his education or training status:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following?**
- Education (such as school or college)
- Approved training (such as an apprenticeship or other recognised training scheme)

Or, has he recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks)?

Please let me know his current situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in education studying for A-levels. Let me check the next requirement:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check that Alex's A-level studies meet the specific requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

**For Alex's A-level education, please confirm:**

1. **Is he doing full-time study** with at least 12 hours per week of supervised study time? (A-levels are typically full-time, so this usually applies)

2. **Is the A-level course employer-funded** or is there an arrangement where he's agreed to work for a specific employer after completing it? (This would typically be "no" for standard sixth form college A-levels)

3. **Is Alex married?** (This would only affect eligibility if he is)

For context, A-levels are on the approved list of qualifications, so as long as he's doing full-time study (12+ hours/week) and it's not employer-funded, he should qualify.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's doing full-time study at the college - it's a proper full-time A-level course. No, it's not employer-funded - it's just standard sixth form college. And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex's A-level education clearly meets the requirements. Now let me check the next criterion:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working, and if so, how many hours per week?**

The rule is that children aged 16+ can work up to 24 hours per week while in approved education and still qualify. If he's working 24+ hours per week, he wouldn't be eligible.

So please tell me:
- Is Alex not working, or does he have a part-time job?
- If he has a job, how many hours per week does he typically work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex does work. He has a part-time job at the local supermarket - it's actually quite a lot of hours, he works full-time there alongside his studies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to clarify this - you mentioned Alex works "full-time" at the supermarket while also doing full-time A-level studies. 

**How many hours per week does Alex work at the supermarket?** 

This is important because the threshold is 24 hours per week. If he's working 24 or more hours per week, he would not be eligible for Child Benefit even though he's in approved education.

Can you give me a specific number of hours, or an estimate?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He works 24 hours a week at the supermarket - so it's basically full-time alongside his college work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, this means Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit.

The rule is that children aged 16-19 who are in approved education (like A-levels) can work, but **only up to 23 hours per week**. Since Alex is working 24 hours per week, he exceeds this limit.

Let me confirm this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Outcome: **INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

### Reason:
Alex is 17 and in approved full-time education (A-levels), which would normally make him eligible. However, he is working 24 hours per week at the supermarket, which exceeds the maximum limit of **23 hours per week** that children aged 16-19 in education are permitted to work while remaining eligible for Child Benefit.

### What this means:
- Child Benefit stops when a 16+ year old works 24 or more hours per week while in approved education/training
- Even though Alex is in approved education, his work hours push him over the threshold

### Next steps:
If Alex reduces his working hours to **23 hours per week or less**, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him again. You would need to contact HMRC to restart your claim once his circumstances change.

I understand this may not be the outcome you were hoping for. If you have any questions or if Alex's situation changes (such as reducing his work hours), please feel free to come back and we can reassess.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and in approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college), which normally qualifies for Child Benefit. However, he is working 24 hours per week at his supermarket job. The eligibility rules state that children aged 16-19 in approved education can work, but only up to 23 hours per week. Since Alex is working 24 hours per week, he exceeds the maximum permitted hours and is therefore ineligible for Child Benefit.
